The circle of 5thstap a key

Level 2 · Voicing and voice leading · how chords are spaced, and how each voice moves

Voices

The same chord can be spread, stacked or thinned in many ways. Choose a voicing, hear it, then watch how good voice leading moves every part the shortest way home.

Voicing lab

Voice-leading coach

Same chords, two ways. Block plays every chord in root position, so the voices jump together. Smooth moves each voice to the nearest note of the next chord.

Block
Smooth

Parallels are counted between chords with the same number of notes. Smooth voicing keeps movement small but doesn't apply the strict rules: that's the job of the four-part checker below.

Four-part writing (SATB)

Soprano, alto, tenor and bass, each within its real singing range. The checker marks every rule from traditional part-writing. Click any note, then use ↑ and ↓ to move it to the next chord note: try to break a rule, then fix it.

Level 3 · Compose · thirteen climbs from the first drone to the fugue

The Climbs

Each climb follows the same path: ask, hear, understand, see, try, make. All thirteen climbs are open.

AskHearUnderstandSeeTryMake
Level 3 · Compose · the shapes music is built in

Forms

How a piece is laid out in time: sections, repeats, keys and arrivals. Each form follows the same path as the climbs: ask, hear, understand, see, try, make.

Level 3 · Compose · looking closely at real music, and at your own

Analysis

Scores with switchable layers of analysis, a report on your own progressions, and listening maps for any recording. Every judgement is labelled with the tradition it comes from.

Level 3 · Compose · hear it before you write it

Ear Lab

Seven drills, from the beat to cadences in real scores. Every question is generated and marked by the same engines that run the rest of the Gym, so the answers always match what you hear.

The Gym · build a progression, climb it, hear every voice move

Progression Playground

Choose a key, add chords, and listen. The climbing frame shows how each voice steps from chord to chord. (The playback voicing is a listening sketch, not a model voicing: for strict four-part writing, use Voices.) When it says what you want it to say, take it into your composition software.
